changeset-claim-re-read

## ⚠️ 6 pending changeset(s) describe a file this change touches

Their bodies publish **verbatim** into the CHANGELOG at the next release, so this is a request to **re-read them against your diff** — addressed here because you are the one seat that can answer it without re-deriving anything.

⛔ Nothing here blocks, and nothing here is a verdict on your change. This gate exits 0, is not a required context, and judges **name resolution, never meaning**: it asked whether a pending body names a file you touched. "Is this sentence still true?" is the one question it will not answer, and the one you are being asked to answer.

### `.changeset/10183-date-only-shared-parse-step.md`

- names `utils/date-display.ts` → `packages/core/src/utils/date-display.ts` — edited by this change

  > **Clause-②: yes** — `@object-ui/core` gains one export, `toDisplayDate(value)`: the parse step every date formatter in `utils/date-display.ts` already went through, now reachable by a caller that formats with its own `Intl` options or compares a value with today. Nothing else is added, removed, renamed or retyped, and `@object-ui/fields` does not re-export it.

### `.changeset/6475-gantt-block-face-declared.md`

- names `plugin-gantt/src/ObjectGantt.tsx` → `packages/plugin-gantt/src/ObjectGantt.tsx` — edited by this change

  > The `gantt` nested-block spelling of a gantt config (`{ type: 'object-gantt', gantt: { … } }`) had **no mirror entry at all**: it rode through `BaseSchema`'s `.passthrough()` entirely unvalidated, and the published TypeScript never taught the shape either — an author writing `gantt: { … }` got no completion, no type checking, no error on a misspelt member. It was the 28th and last of the keys `getGanttConfig` (`plugin-gantt/src/ObjectGantt.tsx`) reads off the schema that objectui#6051 (PR #6472) did not declare — severed into its own card because, unlike the other 27, declaring it changes what a published tool refuses.

- names `content/docs/plugins/plugin-gantt.mdx` → `content/docs/plugins/plugin-gantt.mdx` — edited by this change

  > Maintainer ruling, objectui#6475 (2026-08-27), **Option A** — enforce as-is, immediately, no warning window (the startup-stage no-gradualism rule, objectstack#12668: transitions do not get phased windows without named external-user evidence, and none exists here). A census of every `gantt` block reachable through `ObjectGanttSchema` in this repository — the `examples/schema-catalog` fixtures, `content/docs/plugins/plugin-gantt.mdx`, and the published `skills/objectui/guides/page-builder.md` guide — found **zero** blocks missing the trio.

### `.changeset/6939-objectql-record-source-refinement.md`

- names `plugin-gantt/src/ObjectGantt.tsx` → `packages/plugin-gantt/src/ObjectGantt.tsx` — edited by this change

  > Both renderers resolve their records from one of three keys, in this order — `getDataConfig` in `plugin-map/src/ObjectMap.tsx` and `plugin-gantt/src/ObjectGantt.tsx`: `data`, then `staticData`, then `objectName`. Both mirrors required `objectName` alone, so a document authored on `staticData` drew correctly and was refused by `safeValidateSchema` — six catalog entries, three per component.

### `.changeset/7178-format-measure-date.md`

- names `utils/date-display.ts` → `packages/core/src/utils/date-display.ts` — edited by this change

  > **No second date formatter was written.** `formatDate`, `formatDateTime`, `formatRelativeDate` and `DateDisplayOptions` MOVED from `@object-ui/fields`' barrel down into `@object-ui/core` (`utils/date-display.ts`), which is the same remedy objectui#4576 applied to `formatDisplayNumber` and for the same reason: `core` is the React-free engine and could not import from a React package, so the alternative was a parallel date convention in `dataset-format.ts` — exactly the drift that once had a list cell rendering `1.234,5 %` beside a dashboard measure's `1.234,5%`. `@object-ui/fields` re-exports all four names unchanged, so no consumer's import path or behaviour changes, and a reference-identity test pins that the cell renderer and the measure formatter call the same function.

### `.changeset/9786-detail-timestamps-display-locale.md`

- names `machineLocaleCensus-9909.test.ts` → `packages/i18n/src/__tests__/machineLocaleCensus-9909.test.ts` — edited by this change

  > **Two instruments land with the repair, because the repair alone is what happened the last five times.** `detailTimestamps.displayLocale-9786.test.tsx` renders every surface whose face reaches the DOM under a declared `de-DE` session and a declared `en` one and requires the two readings to differ — an assertion the runner's own locale cannot satisfy, since before this change both legs came from the machine and were byte-identical whatever the machine was. It also patches the `Intl` constructors and `Date.prototype.toLocale*` and inspects the argument each call actually receives, which is the only way to catch a variable that resolves to `undefined`, and the only way to reach `RecordMetaFooter` — whose absolute face is a `TooltipContent` child that Radix keeps out of the DOM until the tooltip opens. A census pin reddens when a new bare, `undefined`- or hard-coded-tag call site is written; it masks comments before it counts, and when it landed it declared `InlineFieldInput`'s `en-CA` as an exemption with its reason — that call fed `ANGLE-BRACKETS(input type="date")`, whose value HTML defines as `YYYY-MM-DD`, so it was an ISO formatter and not a display locale. It landed scoped to this package and, under the ruling on this card, became the one repository-wide census in `@object-ui/i18n` (`machineLocaleCensus-9909.test.ts`, objectui#9909), which carried that exemption forward. objectui#10625 later removed the call: `InlineFieldInput`'s date editor now renders `@object-ui/fields`' `DateField`, and the exemption went with it.

### `.changeset/9909-machine-locale-sweep.md`

- names `machineLocaleCensus-9909.test.ts` → `packages/i18n/src/__tests__/machineLocaleCensus-9909.test.ts` — edited by this change

  > **One census, repository-wide.** `plugin-detail`'s machine-locale census pin (objectui#9786) is now a single test, `machineLocaleCensus-9909.test.ts` in `@object-ui/i18n`, covering every workspace package whose manifest depends on `@object-ui/i18n`. It refuses any call site that passes nothing, `undefined`, the `'default'` pseudo-tag (a subtag no locale data answers, so `Intl` resolves it to the machine's locale) or a hard-coded tag, unless the site is declared with its reason — for example the `catch` fallback for a tag `Intl` itself rejected, or an ISO formatter feeding `ANGLE-BRACKETS(input type="date")`. Each declared site is counted exactly, so deleting one without its entry is refused too. The per-package pin it replaces is deleted. The runtime tripwire that observes the argument each locale-taking call (`Intl` constructors, `Date` and `Number` `toLocale*`) actually receives moved into the private `@object-ui/test-support` package, and every surface above is pinned with it: the same data under two declared locales must render differently, NO locale-taking call may receive the machine's locale (nothing, `undefined` or `'default'`), and the surface's own calls must receive the declared tag. A call carrying another declared tag, such as the `'en'` of the session's UI language, is tolerated by design: only the machine's locale is the defect.

Read the **paragraph**, not the line: both false halves of the objectui#8617 claim sat in one paragraph, and correcting either alone would have left it asserting the same wrong thing.

If a claim did go false, **correct the body**. That is precedented and prose-only, frontmatter untouched; `check-changeset-overwrite.mjs` will report the correction as its own case 2 ("correcting a declaration on purpose … legitimate"), which is the intended shape — one gate asks for the read, the other records the write.

Not covered, stated so nobody reads this as more: a born-false claim that spells no line address at all (objectui#9495 coordinated one by ORDINAL — "a grep finds that member first" — and deciding that means reading what the sentence means), a claim spelled as a symbol or a package rather than a backticked file name, and a file named ambiguously.

Angle-bracketed names in the quoted prose above are rewritten as `ANGLE-BRACKETS(name)`: GitHub deletes tag-shaped fragments from a stored body, and a quote that silently loses the identifier it is about is worse than a visible repair.

Compared the checked-out tree with `3a0e7ab05` (merge-base with origin/main): 15 file(s) changed outside `.changeset/`, read against 1778 pending declaration(s) that publish a body (2384 pending in total). · [run](https://github.com/objectstack-ai/objectui/actions/runs/36646074233)

## Contract review

Served-tier: `CONTRACT_REVIEW_TIER`
Head-sha: `cf8d5aa3cc751637106c95d10997e848ee1d639e`
Local-runs: none

Inputs: card #11141 (body; triage `5898713114`; claim `5899996422`; os-dev-report `5900932893`), PR #11155 (body, the 16-file list, the net diff against `main` at `d71d972ae`), and the check-runs on the head read with `filter=latest`. Read for context, not run: the merge-base `date-display.ts`, `renderer.tsx`, `ObjectGantt.tsx` and `tzShift.ts`; core's `index.ts` and `package.json` at the head; the pending changesets `10183-date-only-shared-parse-step.md` and `11112-timeline-gantt-inclusive-end.md` and core's `CHANGELOG.md` at the head, for the level precedent.

Check-runs on the head: 43 latest runs, all completed: 40 success, 3 skipped (`Test (coverage)`, the coverage shard, `dependabot`), none failed. Every derived gate family is green, `Type Check`, `Lint`, the eight test shards, `Doc Snippet Type Check` and `README Export Check` included, which answers the two NOT MEASURED lines in the report.

### ① Derived judgments

Every accept-set and public-surface change the diff implies, each judged:

1. `@object-ui/core`'s root entry gains TWO value exports, `toDisplayEndDate(value)` and `toInclusiveEndDay(end)`, through the existing `export * from './utils/date-display.js'` in `index.ts` and the package's single `"."` export (`./dist/index.d.ts`). Reachable from the entry type graph and addressable through the exports map, so PUBLISHED surface under this review's own rule. Judged: the additions are RIGHT for the card (one rule in one place, exactly what triage `5898713114` ordered, and ablation G shows that one core line reds both surfaces); their DECLARATION is wrong, see ② and finding 1.
2. `toDisplayEndDate` and `toInclusiveEndDay` are exact inverses on a date-only end: `toInclusiveEndDay(toDisplayEndDate(d))` lands on `toDisplayDate(d)`'s instant for every day tried, the two either side of a skipped midnight included (pinned in `date-display.inclusiveEnd-11141`, real zones read from child processes). The `setHours(0, 0, 0, 0)` after the `setDate` step is necessary and right: the day whose own midnight is skipped (Santiago `2026-09-06` starts at 01:00) would otherwise end at 01:00 of the 7th and name the 7th back. The date-only split is `isRealCalendarDate` on the value's own shape, exactly `toDisplayDate`'s split; an instant, a number or a `Date` is handed back untouched and an impossible day stays Invalid. The inverse (one millisecond back, then the day's floor) names an end inside a day as that day and a midnight as the day before, as the card requires. Judged RIGHT.
3. `plugin-timeline` `readGanttBarEnd`: a string now reads through `toDisplayEndDate`; a number or a `Date` keeps `readGanttDate`'s own read. For a string the base was `toDisplayDate` then `DAY_AXIS.step`, so the two agree on every input except the viewer-local skipped-midnight day (③ item 6). No second copy of the step remains in the renderer. No timeline test file is in the diff: the timeline's pins are unchanged, as the direction requires. Judged RIGHT.
4. `ObjectGantt` `readTaskEnd` for `end` and `baselineEnd`: `toDisplayEndDate`, then `invertTo` exactly as a start takes it. On the identity shim (no `timeZone`) it is the helper's instant, so `scheduling.ts`'s exclusive end instant is now the helper's without `scheduling.ts` moving. The skipped-midnight guard (when `chartZone.to(handed)` is not `end`, hand over `invertTo` of the instant one millisecond before `end`) is a no-op for every chart zone whose clock does not step at 00:00, and for `America/Santiago` it ends the bar at the last instant drawn on its own day so the inverse names the stored day. Pinned in the forks-driven Santiago block of `zonedDstDay-10866`. Judged RIGHT.
5. `toStoredDateValue(..., edge)`: an `'end'` edge on a date-only field writes `toInclusiveEndDay(invertFrom(chartZone, date))`; a `datetime` field still writes `toISOString()`; with no declared type the stored value's shape decides, the same split the read makes. The exact inverse of item 4 on the identity shim and on a zoned chart. `ObjectGantt.endRoundTrip-11141` drives the real view with pointer events: a left-edge drag writes `2024-01-15` back as `2024-01-15`, a move writes both days plus three, a right-edge drag back to the start day writes a one-day task, and a `datetime` control keeps its instant to the millisecond; all three zone pins gain the handed-straight-back case. Stored data does not shift. Judged RIGHT.
6. `GanttView` (an exported component of `@object-ui/plugin-gantt`): the End cell, the row sublabel, the tooltip, both drag previews and the inline editor's seed now name `endDayOf(start, end)` (`toInclusiveEndDay(end)` for a span with length, `end` itself for a zero-length span), and the editor commits through `endOfTypedDay`. `styleFor`, the drag arithmetic and `scheduling.ts` are untouched, so the half-open instants stay as the direction requires. Judged INSIDE the card: the card itself says the tooltip duration changes by one day, the direction says the end pins are re-derived, and ablation C shows the End cell reading the 16th and the editor storing the day before a typed day without this. The accept set is unchanged (the same `GanttTask`); the observable output changes for an embedder that passes `Date` ends directly, the changeset says so, and `GanttTask.end` is now documented as the exclusive instant. Judged RIGHT.
   Residual edge, named and not failed: `endOfTypedDay` keys on the PRE-edit span.
